evidence: app/next.config.ts:7 — the only modern-surface knob is `turbopack: { root: __dirname }`; the top-level `turbopack` key is stable since 15.3.0 and Turbopack is the default, stable bundler since Next 16.0 (nextjs.org/blog/next-16)
app/app/layout.tsx:7 — `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, an App Router API stable since Next 13.4
app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:13-15 — async `params`/`searchParams` promises and `generateMetadata`, the required-and-stable form since Next 15
app/lib/api.ts:20 — plain `fetch` with `cache: "no-store"`; runtime caching is a hand-rolled in-memory Map (app/lib/api.ts:11), no `use cache`/`cacheLife`/`revalidateTag` anywhere
app/components/Filters.tsx:1 — client components use only `usePathname`, `useRouter`, `useState`, `useEffect`, `useRef`; no `useOptimistic`, `useActionState`, or other newer React/Next hooks
grep across app/ — zero `unstable_`/`experimental_` identifiers, zero experimental config flags, no `middleware.ts`/`proxy.ts`
reach.rationale: The app reaches only for long-stable App Router primitives; even the config file avoids anything flagged experimental. The single turbopack option used has been stable config since 15.3.

evidence: app/next.config.ts:1-10 — the entire build-tool surface is one 10-line config, isolated from app code
app/lib/api.ts:1-57 — all data fetching is behind one module (`get`/`find`/`list`), so any future migration to Cache Components or `revalidateTag` would touch one file
app/components/Filters.tsx:11-14 — client-side state/URL logic is confined to two small components, not spread across pages
containment.rationale: There is essentially nothing risky to contain; the one build-level setting lives entirely in next.config.ts and all data access funnels through lib/api.ts.

evidence: app/next.config.ts:7-8 — `turbopack.root` is set with a documented reason (repo-root lockfile vs self-contained app) and matches the docs' guidance for non-standard project layouts

app/app/layout.tsx:6-7 — comment explains why `force-dynamic` is used: every page reads live API data, matching SPEC.md's 'all data from the API at request time' rule — this is the correct stable tool, and skipping Cache Components (recommended for new apps only as of 16.4, nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4) avoids a model still slated to change defaults in Next 17
app/lib/api.ts:7-8 — hand-rolled TTL cache (60s, 5k entries) satisfies the spec's 'caching in memory at runtime is fine' without depending on Next's changing data-cache semantics
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and the modern-but-optional choices it does make (turbopack root, force-dynamic over Cache Components) each have a concrete, documented justification tied to the spec.

findings.issue: `cache: "no-store"` on fetch is redundant in Next 15+/16, where fetch is uncached by default; it also quietly bypasses any future per-request caching semantics.
findings.suggestion: Drop the option and rely on the default uncached fetch, keeping the explicit in-memory TTL cache as the single caching layer.

findings.issue: The app pins next 16.4.3 but does not opt into Cache Components, which Vercel recommends for all new apps as of 16.4 and will become the default in Next 17 — a future-migration consideration, not a defect today.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep as-is for this spec (live data at request time); when upgrading to Next 17, revisit `force-dynamic` + the manual cache against the then-default Cache Components model.

findings.issue: `compress: false` is a minor behavioral dependency on the documented proxy assumption; harmless but worth a comment tying it to the deployment assumption it encodes.
findings.suggestion: It already has a comment; optionally note it mirrors SPEC.md's 'reverse proxy handles compression' so future maintainers don't re-enable it.

summary: This is a maximally conservative App Router app: zero experimental, preview, canary or recently-unstable APIs, with all routing, data fetching and client state built on primitives stable for two-plus years. The only modern-surface choices — a Turbopack config option and the decision to stay on force-dynamic rather than adopt 16.4's recommended Cache Components model — are both deliberate and justified by the spec's live-data requirement. Risk of framework-driven breaking changes is about as low as a Next.js app in 2026 can get, at the mild cost of a Next 17 migration waiting in the wings.

experimentalApis.since: 15.3.0 (renamed from experimental.turbo); Turbopack default/stable bundler since 16.0.0 (2025-10-21)
